Monitor overview
Feedback
Summarize this article for me
Note
Features in this article are powered by the
standard harness
, which uses the billing options described in
Licensing for agents powered by the standard harness
. Learn how to access standard features in
Access standard agents and agent flows
.
Use analytics to understand how well your agent is performing and to identify areas for improvement.
The
Monitor
page in Copilot Studio shows you comprehensive data for your agent, from an overview of key metrics to in-depth usage analytics for your agent's components. You can drill down into each piece of data to get more details.
The Monitor experience is tailored for
conversational agents
and for
autonomous agents
.
Monitoring is available in all geographies. Monitor data is available for up to 360 days. Session details and transcript information are available for the last 28 days. Time-and-date stamps in analytics are in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). The time-and-date stamps include day start and end times, session times, and any other time markers in your agent's data.
Note
The
Monitor
page doesn't show analytics for activity you complete when you test your agent in Copilot Studio by using the
test panel
.
Grant limited view-only access to analytics
If you're the agent owner and want to grant access only to the
Monitor
page of your agent, you can do so by sharing the agent with the
Analytics Viewer
sharing role enabled. If you want the person you're sharing the agent with to have access to information from the conversation transcript, they must also have the
Bot Transcript Viewer
security role.
Learn more about
sharing an agent's analytics
.
Important
As an agent owner, you can only share the Analytics viewer role with individuals and not with groups of users.
To access the
Monitor
page of your agent:
Open your agent in Copilot Studio.
Select
Monitor
on the top menu bar.
Summary
The
Summary
area uses Copilot to generate an AI summary of key analytics insights about your agent. Select
View More
to see the full summarized list of insights.
It helps you quickly understand common themes and metrics and identify areas for improvement for your agent by summarizing them in a bulleted list for the selected reporting period. This can include engagement metrics, customer sentiment and feedback, and trends since the last reporting period.
The
customer comments summary
(preview) helps you understand high-level customer sentiment about the agent, such as feedback and comments. Insights are prioritized based on both the volume of related comments and their overall significance. Low-value or irrelevant comments are filtered out and related feedback are grouped together.
You can provide feedback to Microsoft about this section with the
Thumbs up
and
Thumbs down
icons
. Use the
Submit feedback to Microsoft
panel to add a comment and share related files. By providing descriptive feedback like this, we can work together to continuously improve our product.
On the
Submit feedback to Microsoft
panel, describe in natural language your likes or dislikes, depending on which icon you selected to open the panel.
Choose whether to share prompt, generated response, relevant content samples, and additional log files.
Select
Submit
.
You can also check a high-level performance summary in the
Overview
area, then dive deeper into its performance.
Active users
Active user metrics provide insight to the degree in which a conversational agent is being adopted and how that trends over time. An
active user
is a unique user who interacted with the conversational agent at least once during the report's period. The Monitor tab displays active user counts for two predefined time periods: daily active users (DAU) and monthly active users (MAU). The daily count starts and ends according to a full 24-hour day in the UTC time zone. The monthly count follows the calendar month, also starting and ending on the first and last days according to the UTC time zone.
Important
The
Active user metrics
feature is only supported if you set your agent to require authentication under
Settings
>
Security
>
Authentication
.
The average DAU for the selected period, plus its percent change from the previous period, appears as a key performance indicator (KPI) in the
Overview
section.
Note
The formula for the average DAU calculated metric is:
(sum of all full-day active user counts in the period) / (count of full days in the period)
.
To see more details about daily and monthly active user counts as they trend over time, select the
See active users
button in the top right corner of the overview panel.
Conversational sessions only
Analytics for conversational agents
in Copilot Studio track user engagement with your agent and try to capture how well your agent handles user tasks.
Conversational analytics uses the following concepts and terms:
Conversations are an ongoing interaction between a specific user, or group of users, on a
channel
and your agent.
Conversations can pause and resume later, or be
transferred to a customer service representative
. The conversation might be one-way, either from the customer to the agent, or from the agent to the customer, but it's more commonly a back-and-forth interaction between the customer and the agent.
A conversation times out after 30 minutes of inactivity.
For agents published to the Telephony channel, conversations time out 3 minutes after an
End Conversation
event.
A single conversation can contain one or more analytics sessions.
An analytics session in classic mode is associated with the last custom topic triggered by a user. If the session doesn't include custom topics, it's the last system topic triggered directly by the user.
Event trigger sessions only
An autonomous agent is an agent with an event trigger. These agents support only
analytics for agents with triggers
.
An
analytics session
for agents with triggers tracks from when an agent receives a payload from a trigger through any actions the agent runs in response. These analytics sessions capture what your agent is responding to, and how well your agent performs.
Note
If a trigger fails and the agent doesn't receive a trigger payload, an analytics session can't begin. Analytics tracks only successfully triggered runs.
Hybrid view - both conversational and event-triggered sessions
When your agent's data includes sessions for at least one conversation and at least one trigger-based run in the report's period, the
Monitor
page displays a
hybrid
view of relevant metrics for both conversational and autonomous sessions. In this view, the
Overview
and
Effectiveness
sections show metrics side by side for both the conversational and event-triggered sessions. The
Use
section allows you to select between
Conversations
or
Runs
, which displays only relevant data. Selecting
All
shows all use-related data. The
Satisfaction
section displays satisfaction metrics for conversational sessions.
For more information about:
Displayed metrics relevant to conversation sessions, see
Monitor conversational agent effectiveness
.
Displayed metrics relevant to event-triggered sessions, see
Monitor autonomous agent health
.
Download conversational transcripts
You can download conversation transcripts a few minutes after the conversation times out. You can download any time period within the last 29 days. You can download them in
Dataverse using the Power Apps portal
and as
session chat transcripts using the Copilot Studio app
. It can take up to an hour after the analytic session ends before the related data appears on the analytics dashboard.
Note
You can't download conversation transcripts in Dataverse on the Copilot Studio app in Teams. To review and export transcripts in Dataverse, you need to sign up for the
Copilot Studio web app
. You can download session chat transcripts by using the
Copilot Studio app
. For more information, see
Download agent session transcripts
.
Topic usage analytics
In Copilot Studio, a topic defines how an agent conversation progresses and represents a portion of a conversation between a user and an agent. The topic Monitor pane shows how an individual topic is performing, including how often it's triggered, how sessions that include it resolve, and how satisfied users are with those sessions. You can use these insights to identify topics that frequently escalate or are abandoned, then prioritize them for improvement. To learn more about topics and how to create them, see
Create and edit topics
.
Note
Topic Monitor is only available for agents in
classic mode
and for topics associated with an
session
. If your agent uses generative orchestration, use
conversation outcomes
and
themes
on the
Monitor
page instead.
To view the topic Monitor panel:
Navigate to your agent's
Topic page
in Copilot Studio.
Select the topic you want to analyze. If no topics are available, see
Create and edit topics
.
In the upper-right corner of the
Topics
page, select
More
(...) >
Monitor
.
The topic Monitor panel shows:
Topic outcomes
: A chart of
session outcomes
,
Escalated
,
Resolved
, and
Abandoned
, for sessions where this topic was triggered. Use this chart to quickly assess topic health. A high proportion of
Escalated
or
Abandoned
outcomes can mean the topic needs improvement.
Total topic use
: A chart of the topic outcomes trend over time. Use this to detect regressions, for example, a spike in Abandoned sessions after a topic was edited or to confirm that recent changes improved resolution rates.
Customer satisfaction score
: A score based on user survey responses from sessions associated with this topic.
Satisfaction score trend
: A chart that shows how the
satisfaction score
changes over time. Use this trend to identify periods where user sentiment declined or improved.
To change the time range, select the time range dropdown at the top of the topic Monitor panel.
